Sliding scale registration: $25-$150
($100 recommended)

What can we learn from our favorite poems? In this craft lab, we'll read and discuss several of instructor Nicole Sealey's favorite poems. Within each, we'll explore the line, imagery, diction, surprise and more. We'll also receive writing prompts related to the poems and the things we learn from them.

All participants will have access to a cloud recording of the craft lab for one month afterward. The recording will be shared within a week following the craft lab.

About our Craft Labs

Our Craft Labs are three-hour webinars offering deep-dives into elements of poetic craft, ranging from formal techniques to approaches to the writing process and revision. These sessions are primarily lecture-based, but often include guided writing activities and end with a Q&A with the instructor. An integral part of our Mentorship Program curriculum, the labs are the only part of the curriculum open to the public. These are open to writers of all backgrounds and experience levels. These are structured as webinars, so attendees will not be on video during the talk but can interact via the chat.

Closed captions for the event will be available via Zoom. To request additional accommodations or more information, please contact us at bkp@brooklynpoets.org. Note that by attending you agree to abide by our community agreements.

Join us at Brooklyn Poets for our annual Poetry Festival from October 2 to 4 at 144 Montague Street or via Zoom, where we'll gather for workshops, craft talks, panels and readings! In the mornings, Fatimah Asghar, Shira Erlichman, Joan Kwon Glass, K. Iver, Angel Nafis and Jon Sands will lead generative workshops devoted to exploring the creative process and writing new material. In the afternoons, we'll have panels including "The Debut” (Ahana Ganguly (Futurepoem), Roberto Carlos Garcia (Get Fresh Books), Hannah Matheson (Four Way Books) & Carey Salerno (Alice James Books)); “Behind the Scenes: Journals & Publishing” (Rob Macaisa Colgate (Foglifter), Heather Gluck (Epiphany), Eugenia Leigh (Adroit Journal) & Mary Sutton (Academy of American Poets, prev. West Trade Review)); and “Being a Poet in the World” (Vanessa Jimenez Gabb, Joan Kwon Glass, Megan Pinto & Kwame Opoku-Duku). We'll end the day with craft talks from Tina Chang, Natalie Diaz and Tongo Eisen-Martin and readings featuring the day's teachers, panelists & more.

Super early registration is now open! Through August 31st, you can save ﻿$70 on in-person or virtual passes. Members save an additional $75 on full festival passes and $25 on single day passes. Passes for individual days will be released in September, in-person availability is dependent on remaining capacity.

]]>Brooklyn Poets Summer Virtual Workshop ShowcaseI’s and You’s (and Why’s): How Pronouns Function in Lyric Poems w/ Jay DeshpandeCraft LabsFri, 07 Aug 2026 18:44:47 +0000https://brooklynpoets.org/events/all/is-and-yous632cb432814e3f299440125f:632e08c989068076ca82f9b9:6a76279f67351664a131dc61 Register

Sliding scale registration: $25-$150
($100 recommended)

Our idea of the lyric poem developed out of song, and that means having a singer. The contemporary lyric in English is predicated on certain assumptions about who speaks, and/or that the poem will present the experience of a unitary sensibility. But what are we really expecting from the “I” in a poem? When do we identify the speaker with the poet (for better or for worse)? And how can we consider the I and you in a poem not just as imagined persons, but as useful elements of craft?

In this craft lab, we’ll explore a range of contemporary poems—by Jorie Graham, Harryette Mullen, Dorothea Lasky, Dawn Lundy Martin, Emily Skillings and more—to better understand how the idea of a speaker works and how we bring our own sense of the interpersonal world to the page as we read. We’ll observe our tendency to read a poem based on the I-you relationship it suggests, or through our attraction to autobiographical detail. And by writing poems that test these assumptions, we’ll question whether the pronouns that populate the page are as real as we think they are.

All participants will have access to a cloud recording of the craft lab for one month afterward. The recording will be shared within a week following the craft lab.

About our Craft Labs

Our Craft Labs are three-hour webinars offering deep-dives into elements of poetic craft, ranging from formal techniques to approaches to the writing process and revision. These sessions are primarily lecture-based, but often include guided writing activities and end with a Q&A with the instructor. An integral part of our Mentorship Program curriculum, the labs are the only part of the curriculum open to the public. These are open to writers of all backgrounds and experience levels. These are structured as webinars, so attendees will not be on video during the talk but can interact via the chat.

Brooklyn Poets Reading Series 11.20.26

  • Friday, November 20, 2026
  • 7:00 PM 8:30 PM
  • Brooklyn Poets 144 Montague Street Brooklyn, NY, 11201 United States (map)
  • Google Calendar ICS

Join us for the Brooklyn Poets Reading Series at 144 Montague on Friday, November 20, featuring poets Rhoni Blankenhorn, Asa Drake & Sampson Starkweather! Free and open to the public, the event will also be livestreamed via Zoom. Doors will open at 6 PM and readings will begin at 7. Book signing to follow.

Register

Note that by attending the Brooklyn Poets Reading Series, you agree to abide by our policies. All in-person attendees for events are currently required to wear masks (regardless of vaccination status) except readers on stage. We will have masks available.

Writing Group

  • Saturday, October 17, 2026
  • 12:00 PM 1:30 PM
  • Brooklyn Poets 144 Montague Street Brooklyn, NY, 11201 United States (map)
  • Google Calendar ICS

Join us Fridays at 3pm and Saturdays at 12pm for one hour of structured writing time with prompts created by the Brooklyn Poets faculty staff followed by an optional 30 minute share out at the end. Prompts will vary week to week and will explore various themes and forms. Visit the registration link below to learn who is leading this month’s group!

You can choose to use our prompts or bring your own work and enjoy the structured time. Note that these do not include instruction (aside from the given prompt) or critique — students looking for critique should register for one of our multi-week workshops.

This writing group is free and open to public. If you have the means to do so, you can donate with your online registration or in-person to help support our programming.
